newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil sells 6.6 bln reais in Treasury papers.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sells 6.6 bln reais in Treasury papers.

text.p: Brazil's Central Bank, on behalf of the National Treasury, raised 6.6 billion reais during an auction of Treasury Notes and Letters, dealers said.
A total of 3.799 billion reais was sold in two series of National Treasury Letters known as LTNs.
A total of 3.316 billion reais of 181-day LTNs, due March 1, 1997, was sold at an overnight call money rate of 2.653 percent a month.
The Central Bank also sold 483 million reais of 365-day LTNs, due September 1, 1997, at a call money rate of 2.62 percent a month.
Dealers said it was the first time the Central Bank had offered one-year LTNs to the financial institutions.
The sale was well received by the market since the Central Bank moved to extend the maturity period of public debt, they added.
Some 2.443 billion reais were sold in National Treasury Notes (NTN) indexed to the variation of Brazil's reference rate (TR).
The notes, due March 1, 1997, pay annual yields of 13.35 percent plus the variation of the TR in the maturity period.

The Central Bank sold a series of NTNs indexed to the variation of the dollar, known as NTN-D. A total of 358 million reais in NTN-D with a maturity period of two years will pay annual yields of 12.39 percent, dealers said.
